headline: Retail fuel prices increased by Tk 20 per litre across all major types
summary: The hike, effective from September 20, comes amid high food prices and global energy shocks, threatening to further drive up inflation and living costs.
details: The government has increased the retail prices of all major fuels by Tk 20 per litre, effective from midnight on September 20. This decision follows a period of high food prices and inflationary pressure on ordinary citizens.

The hike is driven by the international energy situation, including higher crude and refined product prices, disrupted shipping routes, and a weakening taka. The government cited the Middle East conflict and BPC losses of Tk 22,875.66 crore between March and August as key reasons.

Rising fuel costs are expected to to increase the cost of producing and transporting food, fertiliser, and raw materials. This ripple effect is likely to raise prices for essential commodities, hitting low-income families the hardest.

The agriculture sector faces increased costs for irrigation, land preparation, and fishing. Small farmers, unable to secure higher prices for their produce, may see their profits shrink while consumers face higher market prices.

Industries are also under pressure, as unreliable electricity and gas supplies force a dependence on diesel generators. Export industries may see profits and competitiveness drop as they cannot easily raise prices due to global competition.

Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are particularly vulnerable due to lower working capital and older, less energy-efficient machinery. For many, maintaining production or working hours could become difficult.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman reaches New York for 81st UNGA session
summary: The Prime Minister arrived at JFK Airport to attend the United Nations General Assembly, where he is scheduled to deliver a key address on September 24.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at John F Kennedy (JFK) International Airport in New York at 6:20 PM local time. He was accompanied by his wife, Dr Zubaida Rahman, and a delegation of officials.
The Prime Minister was received by the Permanent Representative of Bangladesh to the UN, Irene Zubaida Khan, and the Bangladesh Ambassador to the US, Tareq Md Ariful Islam.
Bangladeshi expatriates, BNP leaders, and activists gathered at the airport and along the route to the Hyatt Grand Central New York hotel to welcome the PM with banners and slogans.

The Prime Minister is scheduled to deliver his address to the UNGA on September 24. His official engagements begin on September 22 with a welcome breakfast hosted by UN Secretary-General António Guterres.
His itinerary includes bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay, and World Bank Group President Ajay Banga.
He will also meet with the UN Secretary-General’s Special Envoy on Myanmar, Julie Bishop, and European Council President António Costa.
On September 23, the PM will join a high-level side event on the Rohingya crisis and a meeting on 'Climate Action and the Just Transition' at the UN Headquarters.
He is also scheduled to meet with Pakistani Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif and deliver opening remarks at an event focused on maternal and newborn health.
The visit concludes with a breakfast meeting with Wall Street representatives hosted by JPMorgan on September 25 in Manhattan.
